P1.rule: each open-weight arm (weights public at freeze) in the cheap-tier band (repeat met on <= 13 of 19) and holds <= 10 of 19

P2.rule: Gemini repeat met on >= 17 and holds >= 15

P3.rule: action_tendency, scope, need are the first to fail 5-of-9 (read: they are in the failing set) AND primary, valence, attribution, bodily_sensation, summary hold across >= 8 of 9

P4.rule: intensity.value null on >= 50 % of texts for >= 3 of the 6 new arms

levers.written: 2026-10-18 after the pilot (plan section 9 gate), revised after each re-pilot; every entry is a deviation logged in RESULTS.md section 0.1 and plan section 12
levers.stop_why: lever 2: after lever 1 the projection was USD 70.0 (> 50), so the stop is raised to 60 and no arm is dropped for being over 50; lever 3 then applied because 70.0 > 60 (see dropped_arms). Lever 4 (2026-10-18, Phase A of the founder's overnight instruction 'finish run 3, cap USD 15'): the stop is raised from 60 to 70 so that judge.py's start rule (remaining >= 9 reserve) and its 10-call projection check do not refuse the seven summary texts that failed on 429 during the resume (spent 44.23 + judge 8.13 left 7.64 under the 60 stop) nor the R30 free-text supplement (judge.py --rejudge, ~USD 7.7, booked to spend_judge.json); the Phase A cap of USD 15 over the 49.35 spent at the close (judge completion + R29 probe + R30 extension + supplement) is enforced separately: judge.py --cap-usd on the supplement, cap_usd 8 on the extension, STATUS.md ledger. Lever 4 amended after the R30 supplement (judge total 17.16 under the 70 stop left 8.60, below the 9-reserve start rule): stop 72 so the 15 texts whose supplement call failed on OpenRouter 429 (12 summary, 3 four-field) can be re-judged under judge.py --rejudge-missing --cap-usd 1.2; the Phase A ledger (cap USD 15) is the binding limit
levers.dropped_why: lever 3: projection after levers 1-2 = 70.0 > 60. The costliest open-weight arm by projection among N2 / N3 / N4 / N6 (N1 never; N5 not open-weight at freeze): N2 DeepSeek V4 Pro 13.32 (mean 0.017762 per call over re-pilot 2) against N3 Qwen3.8 13.31 (0.017741) - a near tie of USD 0.01 on three calls each, decided by the rule as written. Projection without N2: 56.7 <= 60, so no further drop. The 5-of-9 rule reads 5-of-8 (three voters + 5 new arms); the P1 open-weight set is N3, N4, N6
levers.reasoning_low_why: lever 1: measured per-call cost exceeded 1.5 x the section-9 line on arms that expose a reasoning parameter: Qwen 0.0878 vs 0.0103 (reasoning 9.5k-17k tokens per call, 267-450 s), Mistral 0.0229 vs 0.0035 (reasoning 9k-11k; one of three calls hit max_tokens 12,000 with no JSON), gpt-oss-120b 0.00045 vs 0.00022 (reasoning ~1.7k), DeepSeek (first served in re-pilot 1, via StreamLake) 0.0221 vs 0.0033 (reasoning 8.2k-11.6k; one of three hit max_tokens with no JSON). Gemini 0.0128 vs 0.0127 did not qualify. reasoning = {effort: low} sent on every call of these arms and recorded per record. Re-pilot 1: Qwen 0.0177 (reasoning 1.7k-2.1k), gpt-oss 0.00027; Mistral unchanged at 0.0204 (reasoning 8.2k-9.7k: the endpoint ignores effort), so Mistral also got the token-cap form below. Re-pilot 2: DeepSeek at effort low 0.0178 (reasoning 5.8k-10.5k, partly honoured)
levers.reasoning_max_tokens_why: lever 1, token-cap form ('where only a token cap is supported'): Mistral's endpoint lists reasoning_effort but re-pilot 1 shows effort low leaves its reasoning at 8.2k-9.7k tokens; reasoning = {max_tokens: 2400} (the budget OpenRouter would derive from effort low at max_tokens 12,000) is sent instead. Re-pilot 2: the budget is ignored too (reasoning 5.8k-8.5k, 0.0180 per call); Mistral runs at its measured cost (13.5 projected) and, not being open-weight at freeze, is outside the lever-3 drop set
levers.thinking_disabled_withdrawn: Attempted as R3-D2 after pilot 1 (the two Claude arms returned reasoning tokens through the gateway, Haiku 649-1,203 per call, Sonnet 509 on one of three, where the direct API of runs 1-2 billed none). Haiku accepted reasoning = {enabled: false} (3 pilot calls, 0 reasoning tokens, USD 0.0004-0.0009 per call, records kept in raw/pilot); the Sonnet endpoint refused every call with 400 'Reasoning is mandatory for this endpoint and cannot be disabled.' Withdrawn for both Claude arms so that they share one regime, which is the frozen plan's 'provider defaults' through the gateway; reasoning tokens are recorded per call and the framing bound (Q5) is read with the caveat that a thinking-regime difference between run 1 and run 3 may be part of it. The judge tries {enabled: false} first and falls back to the default if the Opus endpoint refuses likewise (recorded per record)

deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813.why: R3-D1: the pinned first-party endpoint `deepseek` is removed at routing time by the OpenRouter account's data-policy guardrail ('Paid model training violation (account settings)'), which the /endpoints listing does not show; all three pilot calls failed with 404 before any token was served. Re-pinned by the freeze's own rule for the no-first-party case: no quantisation stated and the model's listed price (0.66 / 1.98), status 0, uptime 100 at pin time (StreamLake); served 3 of 3 in re-pilots 1 and 2 (provider StreamLake). Moot for the main run: the arm was dropped by lever 3

pilot_history.note: DeepSeek 0 of 3 served (guardrail); Qwen 65.9, Mistral 17.2, Sonnet 14.0 (cache written on every concurrent pilot call, never read), Gemini 9.6, Haiku 1.0, Llama 0.5, gpt-oss 0.3; + judge 9

pilot_history.when: re-pilot 1 (15 calls: DeepSeek via StreamLake; Qwen, Mistral, gpt-oss at effort low; Haiku thinking off; Sonnet thinking off refused, 0 served; USD 0.18)
pilot_history.note: DeepSeek 0.0221 -> 16.6 projected; Qwen 0.0177 -> 13.3; Mistral 0.0204 -> 15.3 (effort ignored); gpt-oss 0.00027 -> 0.2; Haiku (no thinking) 0.0006 -> 0.45

pilot_history.when: re-pilot 2 (12 calls: DeepSeek at effort low; Mistral at reasoning budget 2,400; Haiku and Sonnet at gateway defaults, Sonnet sequential so the cache is read; USD 0.15)
pilot_history.note: Gemini 9.56, DeepSeek 13.32, Qwen 13.31, Llama 0.50, Mistral 13.49 (budget ignored), gpt-oss 0.20, Haiku 1.09, Sonnet 9.53 (cache read on 2 of 3 sequential calls: 0.0075 / 0.0124 against 0.0183 on the write) + judge 9 = 70.0. Gate: lever 2 -> stop 60; lever 3 -> drop DeepSeek (costliest open-weight by 0.01); projection 56.7 <= 60; run starts with 7 arms. Pilot spend total USD 0.77

levers.transport_retry_R3-D3: After the main run 87 Sonnet 5.5 and 60 Gemini 4 Argon records were transport failures: OpenRouter 429 'Rate limit exceeded: new-account-...' after six attempts with backoff (no model answer was produced; usage null; cost 0). A 429 is not a sample, so these (text, repeat) jobs were re-requested once at concurrency 3 (run_extraction_retry429.log); the failed record stays in the checkpoint file and the served record supersedes it in load_outputs (last record per (text, repeat) wins). Mistral's 89 unparsable outputs (max_tokens 12,000 reached inside the reasoning, finish_reason length) are model outputs and stay failed repeats, never re-sampled
levers.credit_ceiling_note: OpenRouter credit USD 50.00 at freeze (0 used). The projection in force (56.7) exceeds the credit, so by the plan's credit-ceiling paragraph (section 9) the run keeps every retained arm and, if the credit runs out, stops checkpointed for the founder to top up and resume; the judge pass starts only if the stop rule allows and stops on its own projection or on exhausted credit
levers.coverage_clause_R3-D4: R3-D4 (logged 2026-10-18 after the run, with ruling R18): the pre-registration coverage clause (plan section 7: a cell with coverage below 50 % of texts, exclusions plus nulls, is uncovered) counted nulls against coverage; written to catch sparse arms, not fields null by design. Applied literally in the frozen scoring (reading (a): every stated-only field uncovered for every arm). R18 adopts reading (b) prospectively - a null-valued answer counts as covered; only invalid outputs and majority exclusions reduce coverage, the run-1 convention under which these fields earned their class - and reading (a) stays reported beside it as the frozen verdict (score.py decision / decision_alt, verdict / verdict_alt; RESULTS.md section 2). Nothing in score.py was changed: the sensitivity column computed before the ruling is the (b) reading
levers.judge_resume_2026-10-18: judge.py resumed on the remaining credit after the founder's close instruction: 6 further calls served (four-field group 124 -> 127 of 150 texts, summary 66 -> 69) before OpenRouter refused every call at 402 with USD 0.52 of the 50 credit left (the gateway reserves the call's maximum cost); 104 calls remain (23 four-field, 81 summary) for the founder to top up and resume; summary's verdict stays a coverage artefact (R20)

extension_plan_R30.why: R30 (rulings-2026-10-18.md): DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813, dropped at the gate by lever 3 on a USD 0.01 projection difference, runs as a one-arm extension with reasoning off under a hard cap of USD 8 on its own spend (spend_extension.json; STATUS_extension.md on a stop) and is added as the ninth model: score.py re-includes it (NEW_ARMS_RUN) once executed is true, and the rule reads 5-of-9. The five free-text fields need judge.py --rejudge (~300 calls, ~USD 7.7; outside the cap, founder's call); until then its free-text cells are uncovered (judge pending). NOT EXECUTED on 2026-10-18: credit exhausted. Command: python -P experiments/2026-10-18-run3/scripts/run_extraction.py --extension; then set executed true, re-run score.py and results_md.py
extension_plan_R30.executed_note: Executed 2026-10-18 (Phase A step 3): 750 of 750 calls served by StreamLake with reasoning {enabled: false} honoured (0 reasoning tokens on every record), 0 parse failures, 0 missing keys, 0 transport failures, 0 provider mismatches; USD 1.27 (0.00169 per call) against the USD 8 cap; 1,660 s at concurrency 4. DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 is the ninth model; the free-text supplement (judge.py --rejudge, every text re-judged with all nine arms' answers; the new records supersede the 8-arm records) ran next under judge.py --cap-usd 9.5 (Phase A ledger)

r29_probe.branch: re-run the arm under these parameters (>= 9 of 10 parsed)
r29_probe.status_after: Branch 1 is triggered (10 of 10 parsed; every call finished with stop; the 8,000 reasoning budget was not honoured, mean 10,300 reasoning tokens, but the 32,000 completion cap left room for the JSON; USD 0.0247 per call). The re-run of the arm under these parameters (750 calls, about USD 18.5 at the probe's measured cost) EXCEEDS the Phase A cap of USD 15 after the judge completion (3.22), the R30 extension (1.27), this probe (0.25) and the R30 supplement (<= 9.5): NOT executed on 2026-10-18; the founder sets the stop (R29: 'the founder sets the stop'). Until the re-run, the arm's run-3 figures stand in the tables flagged 'reasoning-cap artefact confirmed by the probe' and the verdict without Mistral is reported beside as a sensitivity (score.py verdict_wo_mistral; RESULTS.md section 2); the else-branch exclusion is NOT applied (excluded_arms empty) because the probe took branch 1. No field verdict changes either way (R29)

levers.judge_complete_2026-10-18: judge.py resumed after the founder's top-up (OpenRouter credit 100, 49.48 used) under Phase A of the overnight instruction: 104 calls served (USD 3.01; 0 malformed), seven summary texts failed on OpenRouter 429 after three attempts and were served by a second invocation (7 calls, USD 0.21; stop raised to 70 by lever 4 first, because the judge's 9-reserve start rule refused them under the 60 stop). Both groups now cover 150 of 150 texts: 311 billed judge calls, USD 8.34. R20 closes mechanically: summary holds 8 of 8 under both readings (every arm repeat >= 0.89, agree >= 0.73, coverage >= 0.81); harm rises to 5 of 8 under reading (a) (6 under (b)); no other verdict changes. The Opus endpoint refused reasoning {enabled: false} on every invocation (fallback to the gateway default, recorded per record). The 8-arm scoring at this point is kept as scoring/8arm/ and RESULTS.8arm.md before the R30 extension and its supplement change the judge records
levers.field_list_R3-D5: R3-D5 (2026-10-18 Phase A): build_prompts.py derived the 19-field list from the live draft (v09_layout.PROFILES_09['essential']); after R26 moved tether to interpretive (bf97e22) the live tier has 18 and every run-3 script failed on import. The frozen 19 are now pinned in build_prompts.py (FIELDS_FROZEN, the comparable tier at 974408e) and the live tier is asserted to be a subset; the committed prompts are unchanged (build_prompts.py --check passes)
